garlic.note: In the onion (allium) family and toxic to cats, dogs, and horses; it damages their red blood cells.

leek.note: An allium (onion family), toxic to cats, dogs, and horses; it can damage their red blood cells.

onion.note: Toxic to cats, dogs, and horses; onions and the whole allium family damage their red blood cells.

shallot.note: A type of onion (allium), toxic to cats, dogs, and horses; it damages their red blood cells.

spring-onion.note: An onion-family allium, toxic to cats, dogs, and horses; scallions damage their red blood cells.

beefsteak-tomato.note: Ripe tomatoes are fine, but the leaves, stems, and unripe fruit are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

grape-tomato.note: Ripe tomatoes are fine, but the leaves, stems, and unripe fruit are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

heirloom-tomato.note: Ripe tomatoes are fine, but the leaves, stems, and unripe fruit are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

roma-tomato.note: Ripe tomatoes are fine, but the leaves, stems, and unripe fruit are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

eggplant.note: The fruit is fine, but the leaves, stems, flowers, and roots are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses (solanine).

potato.note: The tuber is fine when cooked, but the green parts, sprouts, leaves, and stems are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses (solanine).

tomatillo.note: Ripe tomatillos are fine, but the unripe fruit, leaves, and stems contain solanine and are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

bell-pepper.note: NCSU gives Capsicum annuum no pet-toxicity tag (unlike its nightshade relatives); capsaicin is a mild irritant only. ASPCA's 'Ornamental Pepper' is a different plant (Solanum pseudocapsicum).

banana-pepper.note: NCSU gives Capsicum annuum no pet-toxicity tag (unlike its nightshade relatives); capsaicin is a mild irritant only. ASPCA's 'Ornamental Pepper' is a different plant (Solanum pseudocapsicum).

cayenne-pepper.note: NCSU gives Capsicum annuum no pet-toxicity tag (unlike its nightshade relatives); capsaicin is a mild irritant only. ASPCA's 'Ornamental Pepper' is a different plant (Solanum pseudocapsicum).

habanero.note: NCSU gives Capsicum annuum no pet-toxicity tag (unlike its nightshade relatives); capsaicin is a mild irritant only. ASPCA's 'Ornamental Pepper' is a different plant (Solanum pseudocapsicum).

jalapeno.note: NCSU gives Capsicum annuum no pet-toxicity tag (unlike its nightshade relatives); capsaicin is a mild irritant only. ASPCA's 'Ornamental Pepper' is a different plant (Solanum pseudocapsicum).

apricot.note: The flesh is fine, but the pits, seeds, and leaves contain cyanide compounds and are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

cherry-sour.note: The flesh is fine, but the pits, seeds, and leaves contain cyanide compounds and are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

cherry-sweet.note: The flesh is fine, but the pits, seeds, and leaves contain cyanide compounds and are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

plum.note: The flesh is fine, but the pits, seeds, and leaves contain cyanide compounds and are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

peach.note: The flesh is fine, but the pits, seeds, and leaves contain cyanide compounds and are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

nectarine.note: The flesh is fine, but the pits, seeds, and leaves contain cyanide compounds and are toxic to cats, dogs, and horses.

lemon.note: The fruit is fine, but the peel, leaves, and citrus oils can upset the stomach of cats, dogs, and horses.

lime.note: The fruit is fine, but the peel, leaves, and citrus oils can upset the stomach of cats, dogs, and horses.

orange-navel.note: The fruit is fine, but the peel, leaves, and citrus oils can upset the stomach of cats, dogs, and horses.

grapefruit.note: The fruit is fine, but the peel, leaves, and citrus oils can upset the stomach of cats, dogs, and horses.

mandarin-clementine.note: The fruit is fine, but the peel, leaves, and citrus oils can upset the stomach of cats, dogs, and horses. (mandarin=Citrus reticulata, anchored to the ASPCA orange citrus caution)

lavender.note: Its essential oils (linalool) can cause mild stomach upset in cats, dogs, and horses if eaten.

marigold.source: ncsu:tagetes-patula -- NO pet tag (human phototoxic sap only); safe like Capsicum peppers. NOTE our marigold=Tagetes, not ASPCA's Calendula 'garden marigold'

oregano.note: The essential oils can cause mild vomiting or diarrhea in cats, dogs, and horses if eaten in quantity.

parsley.note: Large amounts contain furanocoumarins that can make skin sun-sensitive in cats, dogs, and horses.

mint.note: The essential oils can cause mild vomiting or diarrhea in cats, dogs, and horses with large amounts.

lemongrass.note: The essential oils can upset a cat or dog's stomach; large amounts can be more serious for horses.

parsnip.note: All parts contain furanocoumarins that can make skin sun-sensitive in cats, dogs, and horses.

bok-choy.source: Brassica rapa, no toxicity listing (non-toxic brassica like B. oleracea)

spinach.source: ncsu:spinacia-oleracea no pet tag (human oxalate only)

pea-shoots.source: garden pea (Pisum sativum) non-toxic (distinct from toxic Lathyrus sweet-pea)

turnip.source: Brassica rapa, no toxicity listing (non-toxic brassica)
